The one named *Śuci*, the self-purifier, the director of the gods, or the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*) who directs those possessing knowledge of sacrifice— along with *Śuci* *kratu*, the beautiful ritual act such as the *agnihotra* and other rites— he was indeed born together; at the very moment of birth, [he was accompanied] by the seven hotṛ-priests.
2. Also [the verses] beginning with *ma* and *aya*.
3. The poems (*kāvyāni*) beginning with *ka*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *dha*, and *va*.
Rigveda [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 26]:
Being the pure director of all, he became the performer of the Agnihotra and other rites; this is the meaning.

At its beginning: the wise sacrificer, knowing the firm and stable vows—meaning the rituals that culminate in their fruit—expands them like branches; that is, he performs them in succession, as branches spread from a tree.
These lowing milch-cows have followed his color as the Neṣṭṛ-priest; surely they are sisters who have come here seeking a boon from those three.
The milch-cows have attached themselves to his color, that of the Neṣṭar priest; do they not indeed prefer him to the three sisters who have joined here? 5.
The fingers (*vyā*), characterized as will be described hereafter, reach toward (*vyuyuḥ*) this rite being performed;
they carry it out.

These fingers—windy (*vāyavaḥ*), fragrant (*gandhyaḥ*), extensive (*vyāsāḥ*), milch-cows (*vdhenavaḥ*), gratifying (*prīṇayinyaḥ*), self-moving sisters (*svasāraḥ*)—[serve] for him who desires the oblation (*neṣṭuḥ*), the one who consumes, the purifier, or the one who partakes, [acting] before that Agni.
Or rather, they repeatedly and constantly attend upon, serve, and worship this [deity] named Ṛtvij, as well as the three forms beginning with Gārhapatya, choosing the most excellent color for them.
When the sister has come near to the mother, bringing clarified butter,
the Adhvaryu, having arrived among them, rejoices like a bull in the rain.
If the sister, bringing ghee, has approached the mother, the Adhvaryu rejoices at their arrival like grain in the rain. 6.

If, when she has become the creator of all, the *juhū*—which is like a sister (*svasā*) to the earth characterized as the sacrificial altar (*vedi*)—stands near, bringing the clarified butter (*ghṛta*), [she] would attend upon Agni.
The singular number is not intended to be significant;
the meaning is that the *juhū* and *upabhṛt* ladles stand there, bringing the clarified butter.

Then, when these [offering ladles], beginning with the *juhū*, have arrived—that is, when they have reached the sacrifice—the officiant named Adhvaryu, desiring the sacrifice (*upadhvara*), says: "This Agni rejoices, he is delighted;
as one rejoices at rain during a drought, so does he."
O Heaven, for your own support, let the priest perform his priestly duty at the proper season;
we have offered praise and sacrifice—may we win them as a gift.

Heaven! For yourself! You who are to be maintained! May [the gods] perform [the rite]. O officiant, [perform] the officiant’s [task]. The hymn and the sacrifice—then may we win them sufficiently; we have offered them. 7.

2. *tha-śobhrāyitu*: to cause to shine; to nourish. 3. 4. jha-1: He approaches the fire.

This Agni, being himself (*svaḥ*) the priest (*ṛtvij*) characterized by the words "the Hotṛ was born," etc., for his own sake (*svāya*)—that is, for his own maintenance (*dhāyase*), or for the holding of the oblations (*haviṣām dhāraṇāya*)—being the lord of priests such as the Hotṛ, Potṛ, and Praśāstṛ, [approaches] the priesthood (*ṛtvijyam*).
This designation is one in which the state (bhāva) is the primary factor.
Being the king of the gods, let him perform the priestly office for the human officiant;
and through his favor, may we immediately thereafter fully and abundantly enjoy the hymn of praise and the sacrifice based upon it,
and may we offer the oblation.
Or rather, may we win the hymn of praise; we have offered the sacrifice and the oblation worthy of sacrifice.
So that the wise man may prepare it well for all the worshipful ones—
this sacrifice which we have performed, O Agni, is centered within you.
So that the wise man may perform service for all the worshipful ones—this sacrifice, O Agni, which we have performed, rests within you. 8.

O Agni, may you favor us in such a way that the sacrificer—being wise, or knowing your own majesty, or skilled in ritual application—may perform what is sufficient (*aram*) for all the gods worthy of worship (*viśvebhyo yajatebhyaḥ*).
We too perform this specific sacrifice (*yam yajñam caṅkumaḥ*);
that sacrifice is indeed for you alone (*tve api*), with *api* having the sense of "only," for the sake of your own pleasure therein.
Therefore, the meaning is that you, O King, acting as various officiating priests, shall carry out that very sacrifice for the sake of all.
The hymn beginning with “imāṃ me,” consisting of eight verses (of which the first six form a *ṣaḍṛca*), is addressed to Agni (*āgneya*), composed by Soma-āhuti, and is in the *gāyatrī* meter.
It is introduced in the *Anukramaṇī* as: “‘imāṃ me gāyatraṃ hi.
Its application (*viniyoga*) is in the *gāyatrī* meter during the *prātaranuvāka* and the *āśvina-śastra*.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: “O Agni, [recite] this fuel-stick for me, this one... [and so on]; from among these three, one should omit the last” (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.13).
During the afternoon *upasad*, the three verses beginning with “*imāṃ me agne samidham*” are to be employed by arranging them extensively to form nine *sāmidhenī* verses.
This is stated in the section titled “Now the *upasad*” as: “But the *sāmidhenīs* are [the verses] beginning with ‘*imāṃ me agne samidham imām*’” (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.8).
O Agni, accept this fuel of mine, this service of attendance;
and truly, hear these songs of praise.
O Agni, accept this fuel of mine; accept this my act of sitting near thee. Hear these songs well! 1.

O Agni, may you accept (*vaner*) this fuel-stick (*samidh*) being placed by me, and this oblation (*āhuti*) which is the means for the *upasad*—or rather, that which is performed during the *upasad* rites.
Likewise, hear (*śrudhi*) these very songs of praise (*giraḥ*) well and thoroughly.
With this [hymn], O Agni, son of strength, we worship you, whose rays are most excellent;
with this well-spoken hymn, O well-born one.
With this [hymn], O Agni, let us worship thee, O Son of Strength, O seeker of horses—with this well-spoken prayer, O well-born one. 2.

O Agni, with this oblation (*ayā*) may we worship and serve you. O child of strength (*ūrjo napāt*), O progeny of *vala*, O seeker of horses (*aśvamiṣṭe*), O pervasive sacrifice!
Alternatively, the horse is the ritual action being performed swiftly;
desiring that [action],
they perform the Upasads while chanting in unison.
"They hastened with their rites; they sacrificed three *sāmidhenī* verses and three deities," so says the Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3.45).
O such Agni, may we worship you with this oblation to dispel your illness.
Likewise, O "Sujāta" (of auspicious birth), may we gladden you with this hymn (*sūkta*), the remainder of the sentence being understood as "with this praise."
Or rather, [it is established] by the statement "disperse," which is augmented by praise.
Thee, who art fond of songs, the bestower of wealth, we who long for wealth worship with our hymns,
O thou worthy of worship.
Thee, who art fond of songs, we who are devoted to worship shall honor with our hymns—Thee, the seeker of wealth, O Giver of Wealth. 3.

O Agni, giver of wealth (*draviṇodaḥ*), we who are desirous of wealth—characterized by oblations (*draviṇasyu*)—and who seek to worship you with songs of praise (*gīrvaṇasam*, worthy of being won through hymns), may we, as those performing service, honor and serve you with our songs of praise.
O wise one, bountiful lord of wealth, giver of riches,
keep those who hate us far from us.
He is the enlightened one, the sage, the bounteous lord, the master of wealth, the giver of riches; do thou drive away from us all enmities. 4.
"O Maghavan, you who are wise, a patron, learned, or an impeller—characterized by such qualities—you, be aware; take heed of our hymn of praise.
Furthermore, O Agni, drive away from us those who harbor hatred."
May he send us rain from heaven; may he send us unassailable booty;
may he send us thousandfold nourishment.
May he [grant] us rain from heaven; may he [grant] us unassailable booty; may he [grant] us thousandfold nourishments. 5.
"That very same Agni, for our sake (naḥ), from the sky (divaspari)—
the word *pari* here reiterating the sense of the ablative—
from the celestial world (dyuloka) and the intermediate space (antarikṣa); and the phrase 'he brings rain' is to be supplied."
May he alone grant us, for our sake, unassailable, immovable, and abundant strength (vāja);
likewise, may that very Agni grant us foods (iṣas) of a thousandfold, that is, of immeasurable varieties.
O most youthful messenger, being praised with our song for the sake of help,
come as the best of sacrificers, O Hotṛ-priest.
To the one who is praised, who seeks our aid, O youngest messenger, most excellent sacrificer, O Hotṛ, come hither with our song! 6.

O Agni, most youthful one, messenger of the gods, indicator of the sacrifice and other rites, most worthy of worship, invoker of the gods: come hither for my sake, through our song of praise, for the one who magnifies you, who seeks your protection, and who desires your favor. Come!
1. Those possessing the six vowels—ka, kha, ga, ca, jha, jha¹, ṇa, ta, tha, na, ma, va—perform the *upasads*.
2. With those [consonants] ka, ca, jha, ṇa, tha, na, ma, va, one should recite the hymn (*stuti*); [specifically] with jha¹ augmented by the hymn and consecrated by the mantra.
3. Kha, ga, ca, ṇa, va are characterized by excellence; jha¹ possesses the quality of being pre-eminent (*uttu*).

O *kavi*, wise Agni, you indeed go (*īyase*)—that is, you move or you know—within the hearts of men.

Knowing both kinds—namely, the births belonging to the sacrificers (the worshippers) and the gods who are to be worshipped—you move along; this is the connection.
In this regard, there is an illustration:
like a messenger who is beneficial to the people (*janyaḥ*) and especially beneficial to friends (*mitryaḥ*).

27. The seventh hymn, consisting of six verses beginning with “*śreṣṭhaṃ yaviṣṭha*,” is addressed to Agni by Soma-Āhuti; it is in the *gāyatrī* meter.
Its application in the *chandas* for the purpose of the *prātaranuvāka* and the *āśvina-śastra* has already been stated in the preceding hymn.
She is employed in the Śrāvaṇī rite.

O Agni, most youthful descendant of Bharata, bring hither the most excellent, radiant, and much-desired wealth, O Vasu! 1. Most excellent; O most youthful one; O descendant of Bharata; O Agni; bring hither; the radiant; O Vasu; the much-desired; wealth. 1.
O Agni, O youngest, O most youthful one! O Bhārata—the descendant of Bharata; for the Bharatas are the officiating priests (ṛtvij), and you belong to them, hence you are the Bhārata.

O *vaso*—O dweller or all-pervading one—you who are thus occupied by the *adhvaryu*s and others through the churning, the oblation, the hymns of praise, and so forth; bring to us that most excellent, highly lauded, radiant, and much-desired wealth.
May neither the malady of the god nor that of the mortal prevail over us. Deliver us from that and from our enemies. (2)
1. *ṇa-ta-tha-va* in the heart, in the heart;
2. *tha-va* for the sake of knowing the mind;
3. *jha-śrāvaṇa*; 4. by means of *jha-pa-va-taiḥ*.
O Agni, by your grace, may *arātiḥ*— meaning non-giving or enmity; or,
since in Vedic usage the word *arāti* is feminine and denotes an enemy—
the stingy enemy, not overcome us (*naḥ*).
May he not be able to overcome;
may he not make [him] an object [of his enmity].
The enemy is thus specified.
Caused by those belonging to both the divine and the mortal;
and furthermore, fill up the deficiency of that twofold enemy of ours.
And through you, may we cross over all enemies, as one crosses a stream of water.
And may we, through you, cross over all our enemies as if crossing streams of water. 3.

Moreover, O Agni, by your grace, may we cross over all haters—even all those who harbor enmity—just as one crosses the streams of water, that is, the small currents connected with water; may we go beyond them by ourselves alone, without depending on anything else.
O Agni, pure, purifying, and worthy of praise, you shine forth mightily;
you are invoked with offerings of clarified butter.
Pure one! Purifier! Worthy of praise! O Agni, you shine forth mightily when you are invoked with offerings of clarified butter. 4.
O purifying Agni, being pure and stainless, and worthy of adoration— that is, fit for homage— you shine forth greatly and intensely, you blaze in various ways;
for you have been offered oblations of clarified butter (ghṛta), being sprinkled with it because of its flowing nature,
and therefore you shine forth.
O Agni, descendant of Bharata, you are ours, having been invoked with offerings of barren cows, bulls, and eight-footed mares.
You, O Agni, descendant of Bharata, are ours; you have been worshipped with offerings of barren cows, bulls, and eight-footed mares. 5.

O Agni, you who stand in the place of a son to the officiating priests, O Bhārata, you have been worshipped and propitiated by us with barren cows, with bulls, with eunuchs, and with eight-footed (pregnant) cows.
The ancient, desirable Hotṛ-priest, the son of strength, the wonderful one, whose protection is like clarified butter, has come.
He whose food is wood, whose drink is clarified butter, the ancient, the chosen Hotṛ-priest, the son of strength, the wonderful one. 6.

Seated upon the wood, drinking the libations, having clarified butter poured into him— he in whom the clarified butter is offered and poured— ancient, the Hotṛ who performs the oblation, most excellent, worthy of being chosen, the son of strength (Sahas),
standing in the place of a son because he has arisen through power,
and wonderful, being a source of marvel.
The meaning is "delightful.

1. *Ka*, *kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *jha*, *ṇa*, *ṇa* [are combined with] *1*, *tha*, *na*, *pa*, *ma*, *va* when they are enemies (*vidviṣ*). 2. *Kha*, *ga*, *ṇa* [are combined with] *1*, *ta*, *pa*, *pha*, *jha*, *a* like a flow of breath (*āśvasrutiriva*); *ka*, *ja*, *jha*, *tha*, *ma*, *va*, *a* like a flow of breath; *na* like a flow of breath; *ca* like a flow of breath; *jha* like a slight flow of breath; *ṇa* like a flow of breath. 3. *Kha*, *ga*, *ca*, *ṇa*, *1*, *ta*, *tha*, *na*, *va* having approached (*abhikramya*).
